summary.text: Lingfield Park is a parkland course in Surrey that runs either side of the Lingfield Park racecourse, opened in 1987.

setting.text: The course is set among 200 acres of Surrey parkland at Lingfield Park Racecourse, with bunkers, streams, ponds and mature trees.
It measures 6,487 yards, par 72, according to Today's Golfer.
Holes four and five run through mature woodland, and the 2nd runs alongside the railway line, according to Golf Monthly.

history.text: The golf club was established in 1987.
A large hotel with spa was added later. It is managed by Arena Racing Company under the Marriott brand.
The course hosted the Surrey PGA Open for three consecutive years.

trivia.text: Golf Monthly's Rob Smith, reviewing the course on its 30th birthday, said it had matured well since it opened.
Players cross the racetrack twice: after the 11th to play the next five holes, and again before the short 17th.

2.text: The par 5 2nd runs alongside the railway line.

3.text: The par 4 3rd is very attractive, with water guarding anything short of the green.

6.text: Golf Monthly calls the 6th perhaps the prettiest hole, played over a pond to a tricky two-tier green.

13.text: The 13th is a pretty par 4 dogleg from right to left, with a ditch to cross on the approach.

15.text: The par 5 15th is an excellent long hole that the really big hitters may try to reach in two.

17.text: The 17th is a short par 4 with out of bounds left of the green and trees and a stream on the right.

18.text: The closing par 5 is short and reachable but narrow, demanding straight hitting.

local.text: The golf course is part of the Lingfield Park Resort in Surrey, alongside the racecourse and the Marriott hotel.
